review: Internal methodological audit only; no independent peer review or new animal experiment

provenance.acquisition: Downloaded from the public Dryad link via normal browser; all 49 records match the independently extracted visible preview.

clownfish.method: Exploratory paired fish-level percentile bootstrap: mean UV-positive minus mean UV-negative threshold per fish, then equal weight across fish
clownfish.limits: Convenience sample; color sets differ and order/learning may confound contrast. Threshold-fit uncertainty and receptor-noise uncertainty are not propagated. Not a reproduction of the paper’s mixed-effects analysis, a causal UV effect, or independent validation.

lens.method: Student t interval for a population mean; df=2; iid normal fish assumed; small sample and rounding limit inference

worm.method: Approximate Fisher-z interval from rounded summary; independent bivariate-normal units assumed

oratosquilla-oratoria.description: Target and background have equal total intensity. Bars show ideal analyzer transmission; screen colors are diagram colors.
oratosquilla-oratoria.method: Iout/Iin = [1 + DoLP × cos(2(θ − α))]/2. Background θ=0°. Ideal optics; no biological gain, noise or perception fitted.
oratosquilla-oratoria.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
oratosquilla-oratoria.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
oratosquilla-oratoria.limits: Analyzer gain and orientation are unmeasured assumptions. Circular polarization and exact retinal organization are not modeled. No polarization is extracted from your camera.

octopus-vulgaris.description: Target and background have equal total intensity. Bars show ideal analyzer transmission; screen colors are diagram colors.
octopus-vulgaris.method: Iout/Iin = [1 + DoLP × cos(2(θ − α))]/2. Background θ=0°. Ideal optics; no biological gain, noise or perception fitted.
octopus-vulgaris.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
octopus-vulgaris.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
octopus-vulgaris.limits: Ideal analyzers omit retinal irregularity, eye movements and alternative intensity cues. The model is not a reconstruction of subjective appearance. Pooled repeated choices cannot supply an animal-level 95% interval.

tyto-alba.description: Physical grating size subtending one cycle at the assumed distance. This is not a detection guarantee.
tyto-alba.method: Period = 2 × distance × tan[(1 / cycles-per-degree) × π / 360]. The 2.6–4.0 range is published observations, not a 95% interval.
tyto-alba.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
tyto-alba.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
tyto-alba.limits: This is a grating-geometry calculation, not object recognition or a night-vision filter. T. alba pratincola is placed in T. furcata in some taxonomies; transfer to this archive specimen is explicitly uncertain. Two animals do not establish a species-wide interval.

vulpes-vulpes.description: Relative template excitation under two equal-photon synthetic bands. Differences are not just-noticeable differences or probabilities.
vulpes-vulpes.method: Unit-integral Gaussian photon bands (SD 10 nm), sampled 300–750 nm at 1 nm; integrate against peak-normalized alpha-band templates. Uniform transmission, equal gain; no beta bands. Peak shifts are assumption tests, not confidence intervals.
vulpes-vulpes.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
vulpes-vulpes.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
vulpes-vulpes.limits: Nominal peak templates omit ocular filters, adaptation, neural processing and receptor noise. Equal photons are assumed. Responses are not discrimination probabilities or perceived colors. UV cannot be recovered from ordinary RGB. Canid behavior is not automatically transferable between species.

amphiprion-ocellaris.description: Relative template excitation under two equal-photon synthetic bands. Differences are not just-noticeable differences or probabilities.
amphiprion-ocellaris.method: Unit-integral synthetic Gaussian photon bands (SD 10 nm), integrated at 1 nm over 300–800 nm against the authors’ published fitted cone curves (U, M1, M2, L). Equal gains; no added ocular filter or neural noise. Shifted curves use linear interpolation, zero outside source support. Curve shifts are assumption tests, not confidence intervals.

curveSource.description: Published fitted four-cone sensitivity curves, not raw MSP records. Source README: UV curve uses an A2 best fit; others A1. Includes the source curve shapes instead of refitting nominal alpha bands.

amphiprion-ocellaris.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
amphiprion-ocellaris.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
amphiprion-ocellaris.limits: Published fitted cone curves replace generic templates for this species, including the source UV curve. Synthetic equal-photon illumination and equal gains are assumed. Ocular transmission and the full receptor-noise model are not fitted here; response differences are not discrimination probabilities. Phone UV remains unmeasured.

chrysemys-picta.description: Inside the reported photopic maximum region; no response amplitude inferred.
chrysemys-picta.method: Distance to the reported closed interval [625,640] nm. No curve or confidence distribution fitted.
chrysemys-picta.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
chrysemys-picta.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
chrysemys-picta.limits: The published maximum region is not a 95% confidence interval. No full action curve, UV channel or photopigment function is reconstructed from its endpoints. Subspecies and adaptation conditions matter.

caenorhabditis-elegans.description: Aversive chemical context selected. Avoidance remains unestimated: no dose-response fit is available.
caenorhabditis-elegans.method: Normalize a user-assigned blue:amber photon ratio. This is a hypothetical input convention, not a conversion of the paper’s calibrated light settings or camera color.
caenorhabditis-elegans.predictionStatus: Computational hypothesis; no independent biological validation
caenorhabditis-elegans.intervalReason: No dataset linking this model to subjective appearance; a 95% accuracy claim is not estimable.
caenorhabditis-elegans.limits: No camera view represents a worm’s visual scene. Photon fractions below are inputs, not a fitted avoidance probability. The correlation interval uses a rounded summary and assumes independent strains; relatedness is not modeled.

audit: Resample 11 fish, not 49 threshold rows or thousands of choices. Neutral rows excluded from the paired UV-positive versus UV-negative comparison.
Bootstrap treats published threshold estimates as fixed. Color-set, order, learning, fitted-threshold error and receptor-noise uncertainty remain unresolved.
Clownfish uses the authors’ published four-cone fitted curves, including the A2-based UV fit. Neural noise, ocular filtering and threshold fitting are not reproduced.
Lens t interval describes a population mean under strong small-sample assumptions; not individual prediction or visual-accuracy confidence.
Worm Fisher interval is from rounded r and n; genetic relatedness may violate independent-strain assumption.
Octopus aggregate choices cannot provide an animal-level confidence interval. Polarization transmission is ideal optics.
Barn owl subspecies/taxonomic scope and photopic luminance retained. Painted turtle action-spectrum maximum is not a pigment peak.
Shore crab thesis identified separately from peer-reviewed papers. One-channel MSP is not proof of absence of other receptors.
No exact animal-view, UV recovery, polarization measurement, chemical sensing or 95% perceptual accuracy is claimed from RGB.
Studies without adequate samples retain an unavailable statistical interval. Independent predictive validation remains pending for all ten sandbox models.
